title: Rh antibodies in pregnancy
what: This blood test shows whether the mother has antibodies against the baby's Rh-positive blood. It is done for women with Rh-negative blood.
why: For mothers with Rh-negative blood: during pregnancy, before the protective shot, and after bleeding or an injury.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: Your partner's Rh factor, if known
Past pregnancies, miscarriages, abortions, or blood transfusions
If you had an anti-D (Rh) immunoglobulin shot, and when
If you had bleeding, a blow, or a fall onto your belly

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. If you are having other tests too, check with the lab.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Your doctor will tell you how many times to test. Usually several times during pregnancy.

prepare.title: Protective shot
prepare.text: Immunoglobulin is usually given at about 28 weeks and after birth. Your doctor decides the timing.

steps: You sit down, and a band is tied above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein into a tube
The band is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
If you feel dizzy, tell the nurse. They will help you lie on your side
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days
If antibodies are found, the doctor will check the baby by ultrasound more often
If there are no antibodies, the doctor will tell you when to get the protective shot
red_flags: Bleeding, a blow, or a fall onto your belly: tell your doctor right away. You may need the protective shot
Severe belly pain or heavy bleeding: call emergency services
The baby is moving much less: see a doctor right away

faq.q: I am Rh-negative. Is that dangerous for my baby?
faq.a: Usually not, if you do your tests on time and get the protective shot. Your doctor watches this throughout the pregnancy.

faq.q: Why the shot if there are no antibodies?
faq.a: It stops antibodies from forming. It protects this baby and future children.

reminders.text: Rh antibody test tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record card.
